subject: Economics
selected_point: Draw a bar chart comparing various expenditures under a fiscal deficit.
posted_prompt: A set of axes is displayed on the screen, with the horizontal axis representing budget category and the vertical axis representing amount. Under conditions of fiscal deficit, a bar chart is created to represent income and expenditure.
high_level_evaluation_guide: Target Concept: Fiscal deficit as a visualizable relational condition, defined as "total government expenditure exceeds total government revenue" within a fixed accounting period. Minimum assumptions: (1) monetary amounts are quantifiable and comparable across budget categories; (2) bar height is a valid visual channel for magnitude comparison; (3) budget-category identity justifies separate, evenly spaced positions along the x-axis; (4) color coding (green=income, red-orange=expenditure) is used consistently and is perceptually distinguishable. Expected Phased Storyline: [Phase 1: Setup] Axes appear: horizontal axis labeled "Budget Category", vertical axis labeled "Amount". [Phase 2: Income Anchor] A green bar rises at the leftmost position, representing income/revenue. [Phase 3: Expenditure Bars] Three or more red-orange bars rise sequentially to the right, each one taller than the income bar, representing distinct expenditure categories that collectively exceed income. [Phase 4: Stable Deficit Signal] The final frame holds with the height difference between the income bar and expenditure bars clearly visible: no numbers, no annotations, no further motion. Visibility Constraints: legible at 1080p; no occlusion; axis labels readable without zooming; color contrast sufficient for the green and red-orange bars to be told apart; all bars fully within frame.
manual:
Fiscal Deficit Expenditure Bar Chart Demonstration Instructions
I. Basic Demonstration Information
Demonstration Title: Bar Chart Visualization of Income vs. Expenditure Under Fiscal Deficit Conditions
Subject: Humanities and Social Sciences — Economics — Public Finance
Demonstration Purpose: To visually demonstrate how a fiscal deficit manifests in a bar chart — specifically, by displaying income (revenue) and multiple categories of government expenditure on a shared coordinate system where the horizontal axis represents "Budget Category" (i.e., the distinct budget items being compared) and the vertical axis represents "Amount" (i.e., the monetary magnitude, serving as the quantitative scale). The chart must clearly show that total expenditure bars exceed the income bar, visually encoding deficit conditions. This supports conceptual understanding of fiscal imbalance, budgetary visualization literacy, and interpretation of public finance data.

II. Demonstration Carrier/Equipment
Core Carrier: Digital charting interface (e.g., clean vector-based 2D plotting environment with no gridlines or decorative elements unless specified); pre-defined dataset comprising one income value and ≥3 distinct expenditure categories (e.g., Education, Healthcare, Defense, Debt Servicing), where sum of expenditures > income.
Auxiliary Equipment: Neutral gray background (RGB 240,240,240); sans-serif font (e.g., Arial, 14pt); axis labels rendered in bold black text; consistent color-coding: income bar = green (#2E7D32), expenditure bars = red-orange gradient (#D32F2F → #EF6C00) to signal fiscal strain; optional subtle deficit annotation ("Deficit = Expenditure − Income") in bottom-right corner.

III. Demonstration Content Description
Layout: A single Cartesian coordinate system appears centered on screen. Horizontal (x) axis labeled "Budget Category" (aligned below axis, centered), vertical (y) axis labeled "Amount" (rotated 90°, aligned left of axis, centered). Both axes extend fully across visible plot area with tick marks but no numeric values shown (to emphasize structural relationship over precise quantification).
State Control: Chart renders in static, non-animated sequence: (1) axes appear first; (2) income bar drawn vertically at x=0 (leftmost position); (3) ≥3 expenditure bars drawn sequentially rightward (x=1, x=2, x=3…), all taller than income bar; (4) final frame holds for ≥2 seconds with clear visual dominance of red-orange expenditure bars over green income bar.
Comparison Baseline: All bars share identical width and spacing; y-axis scale is linear and consistent; no logarithmic scaling or distortion. Height difference between income and tallest expenditure bar is ≥30% of income height — ensuring deficit condition is perceptually unambiguous.

IV. Observation of Core Phenomena
Axes Appearance: A clean pair of orthogonal black lines forms the coordinate system. Horizontal line (x-axis) runs left-to-right, labeled "Budget Category"; vertical line (y-axis) runs bottom-to-top, labeled "Amount". No arrows, no origin marker "(0,0)", but orientation is unambiguous.
Income Bar: Single upright green rectangle, positioned at far-left (x=0), height proportional to revenue value. Uniform fill, no outline, no label on bar.
Expenditure Bars: ≥3 upright rectangles, positioned sequentially to the right of income bar (x=1,2,3), each in warm-toned red-orange hues. All are visibly taller than the green income bar. No overlapping, no stacking — side-by-side comparison only.
Deficit Visual Signal: The collective visual weight and vertical extent of red-orange bars dominate the frame; green bar appears comparatively short and isolated — creating immediate perceptual contrast confirming "expenditure > income".
Stability & Clarity: No flickering, no partial rendering, no occlusion. All elements remain static and fully legible throughout final display. Color contrast ratio (green vs. red-orange against gray background) exceeds WCAG AA standard (≥4.5:1) for accessibility.

V. Summary of Key Knowledge Points and Principles
Core Concept Definition: A fiscal deficit occurs when a government's total expenditures exceed its total revenues (excluding borrowing) within a given period. Visualizing this via comparative bar charts transforms abstract macroeconomic imbalance into an intuitive spatial relationship: longer bars = larger monetary outflows.
Principle of Visual Feature Recognition Comparison: The human visual system rapidly detects relative height differences in aligned vertical bars. By fixing the x-axis as "Budget Category" (a categorical axis identifying each budget item) and the y-axis as "Amount" (a quantitative axis measuring monetary magnitude), the chart enforces a direct, ordinal comparison. The deficit is not calculated numerically but recognized visually via height asymmetry — a standard convention in bar-chart design for comparing discrete categories against a shared numeric scale.
Further Knowledge: Real-world fiscal charts often include borrowing (deficit financing) as a separate bar or annotation; however, this demonstration isolates the core deficit condition (expenditure > revenue) without introducing secondary mechanisms. "Budget Category" (horizontal) and "Amount" (vertical) follow the standard categorical-axis/quantitative-axis convention used in most bar charts, so a viewer familiar with ordinary bar charts can read the chart without any special training.

VI. Demonstration Precautions
Axis Label Fidelity: "Budget Category" must appear only on the horizontal axis; "Amount" only on the vertical axis — swapping labels invalidates the demonstration. Font size and weight must ensure legibility at standard viewing distance.
Color Semantics: Green must exclusively represent income; red-orange hues must exclusively represent expenditures. Use of blue, purple, or gray for any bar constitutes misrepresentation of fiscal signaling conventions.
Bar Count Minimum: Exactly one income bar + at least three distinct expenditure bars required. Two expenditure bars or zero expenditure bars fails the "various expenditures" requirement.
Temporal Integrity: Axes must render before any bars. Bars must appear in left-to-right order (income → expenditure1 → expenditure2 → …). No simultaneous pop-in or randomized order.
No Extraneous Elements: No titles, legends, data values, gridlines, animations, or sound. Chart must be minimal, pedagogically focused, and self-contained.

pg_specification.level_1: No coordinate axes appear; or axes appear but are mislabeled (e.g., 'Amount' on the x-axis or 'Budget Category' on the y-axis); or no bars are rendered; or only a single bar appears; or bars are oriented horizontally instead of vertically; or bar colors bear no relation to income/expenditure (e.g., every bar is the same arbitrary color unrelated to the described scheme).
pg_specification.level_2: Axes appear but at least one required label ('Budget Category' or 'Amount') is missing; or two or fewer bars total appear (e.g., income plus only one expenditure); or all bars share one identical color with no distinction between income and expenditure; or the income bar is missing entirely; or bars overlap each other or are stacked rather than placed side by side.
pg_specification.level_3: Axes are labeled 'Budget Category' (horizontal) and 'Amount' (vertical) and are perpendicular; one income bar and at least three expenditure bars are present, arranged side by side; but bar widths or spacing are visibly inconsistent, or one or more axis labels are hard to read (too small, low contrast, or oddly placed).
pg_specification.level_4: Axes are correctly labeled and perpendicular; exactly one bar (in a distinct color, e.g. green) sits at the left representing income; at least three bars (in a second distinct color, e.g. red-orange) sit to its right representing expenditures; all bars share consistent width and even spacing; labels are legible; only a minor cosmetic flaw remains, such as one expenditure bar rendered in a slightly off hue, or a non-neutral/glary background.
pg_specification.level_5: The chart matches the prompt precisely: axes labeled 'Budget Category' (horizontal) and 'Amount' (vertical); one income bar in a single consistent color positioned at the left; three or more expenditure bars in a second consistent color positioned to its right, evenly spaced, equal in width, arranged side by side with no overlap or stacking; background is neutral and uncluttered; axis labels are bold and clearly legible; no extraneous chart elements (titles, legends, gridlines, or data callouts) appear.

scc_specification.level_1: The chart visually contradicts fiscal deficit: the income bar is as tall as or taller than every expenditure bar; or the color coding is reversed (red-orange used for income, green for expenditure); or the chart depicts unrelated quantities that have no income/expenditure relationship.
scc_specification.level_2: Whether a deficit is shown is unclear: expenditure bars are only marginally taller than the income bar -- e.g., the height difference is no more than about 5% of the income bar's height, too small to read reliably as 'greater than' -- or some expenditure bars are shorter than the income bar while others are taller, so the total picture does not clearly show expenditure exceeding income.
scc_specification.level_3: Every expenditure bar is clearly taller than the income bar, so a deficit is visually readable, but the income-vs-expenditure comparison is weakened by inconsistent visual treatment: for example, only the income bar has an outline while expenditure bars do not, or the bars are not grouped/ordered in a way that makes the comparison immediate.
scc_specification.level_4: Every expenditure bar is clearly and unambiguously taller than the income bar, so total expenditure visually exceeds income; the income/expenditure distinction is reinforced by consistent color coding (one color for income, a different color for all expenditures); the height differences are large enough to be read at a glance without measurement; only a small refinement is missing, such as the height gap being generous for most expenditure bars but only barely sufficient for one of them.
scc_specification.level_5: The deficit relationship is unambiguous and requires no calculation to read: every expenditure bar is clearly taller than the single income bar, with height differences large enough to be obvious at a glance; income and expenditure are consistently distinguished by color; no bar's height or placement suggests a competing or contradictory reading (no expenditure bar appears equal to or shorter than income); the chart's sole visual message (expenditure collectively and individually exceeding income) is legible without labels, numbers, or annotation.

sc_specification.level_1: Axes appear after the bars instead of before; or the bars appear in a scrambled order (e.g., an expenditure bar appears before the income bar); or bars visibly shift position after first appearing; or the two axes are not drawn perpendicular to each other (e.g., visibly skewed); or bar heights change after the bars have already appeared with no clear cause; or the background behind the chart flickers or suddenly changes color partway through.
sc_specification.level_2: Axes and their labels appear with a noticeable, disjointed delay between them; or all bars pop in simultaneously instead of appearing left to right; or the income bar is not aligned to the leftmost position; or bars differ visibly in width or sit on different baselines; or the vertical axis appears asymmetric around the origin for no reason.
sc_specification.level_3: Axes appear fully formed before any bars, and bars appear in the correct left-to-right order (income, then each expenditure bar in turn), and all bars sit on a common baseline; but one small hitch occurs, such as one bar appearing very slightly out of alignment with the shared baseline, brief jitter in the axis labels as they appear, or a very short stutter during the transition from axes to bars.
sc_specification.level_4: Axes render fully and remain stable first; the income bar appears at the left; expenditure bars then appear one at a time moving rightward at a steady pace; all bars share the same baseline, width, and even spacing with no visible drift or rescaling after appearing; the only shortfall is that the final still frame holds for somewhat less than the roughly 2-second pause expected once fully drawn.
sc_specification.level_5: The sequence is fully consistent: axes appear and hold steady, then the income bar appears, then each expenditure bar appears in turn moving rightward, ending in a held final frame with no further changes; the axes remain perpendicular throughout; all bars sit on one shared baseline with visibly even spacing and matching width; no bar appears, disappears, jumps, or resizes outside of its single appearance moment; the background stays neutral and unchanged throughout with no flicker or color shift.

Meets any of the following criteria: blurry image; severe flickering, completely incomprehensible; frequent distortion of the shape of people or objects; frequent distortion of the motion trajectory of people or objects; object properties severely violating physical laws; frequent and significant fluctuations, frame drops, or jumps in frame transitions.

subject: Computer Science
selected_point: Demonstration of the Execution Process of Sequential Search Algorithm
posted_prompt: A concise 2D animation illustrates an array of numbered boxes arranged horizontally (e.g., [5, 1, 2, 4, 3]), with a highlighted pointer moving from left to right to perform a sequential search for a target value (e.g., 4).
high_level_evaluation_guide: Target concept: Sequential search, a deterministic, linear, index-ordered traversal algorithm that compares elements one-by-one until first match. Minimum mechanistic assumptions: (1) array is static and unsorted; (2) search proceeds strictly left-to-right by index; (3) termination occurs immediately upon equality detection; (4) no implicit memory or backtracking. Phased storyline: [Phase 1: Static setup. Array [5,1,2,4,3] and "Target: 4" banner displayed.] → [Phase 2: Initiation. Pointer appears at index 0 (5), pulses, compares "5==4? → false".] → [Phase 3: Iteration. Pointer advances to 1→2→4, each with identical compare-false feedback.] → [Phase 4: Termination. Pointer lands on 4, triggers synchronous green pulse + "4==4" confirmation + "FOUND" badge.] → [Phase 5: Completion. Animation holds final state for ≥0.5s. Visibility constraints: All numbers and pointer must be legible at native resolution; no occlusion; perspective is strict 2D front-facing orthographic view; no camera motion or zoom.
manual:
I. Basic Demonstration Information
Demonstration Title: Sequential Search Algorithm Execution Process Demonstration
Subject: Engineering - Computer Science - Algorithms
Demonstration Purpose: To visually demonstrate the step-by-step execution of the sequential search algorithm on a fixed-size array, highlighting the left-to-right traversal pattern, element-by-element comparison, and termination upon first match; to reinforce understanding of linear time complexity and deterministic control flow.
II. Demonstration Carrier/Equipment
Core Carrier: 2D animated schematic — horizontal row of 5 uniformly sized, bordered, rectangular boxes containing integers [5, 1, 2, 4, 3]; a movable pointer (e.g., downward-pointing red triangle); persistent target indicator (e.g., banner "Target: 4").
Auxiliary Equipment: Clean white or light-gray background; sans-serif numeric labels (size ≥24pt, high contrast); frame rate ≥30fps; total duration ≤10s.
III. Demonstration Content Description
Layout: Array centered horizontally; pointer begins aligned with leftmost box (value 5); target banner placed above array.
State Control: Pointer advances strictly left-to-right, one box per step; dwell time per box = 0.6s; upon reaching value 4 (third box from right, index 3), pointer pauses 0.8s while matched box pulses green and displays "MATCH!"
Comparison Baseline: All boxes identical in size, spacing, fill (white), border (black, 2px), and font; only numeric content and pointer state vary.
IV. Observation of Core Phenomena
Pointer Motion Pattern: Smooth, discrete, sequential translation — no interpolation errors, no skipping, no reversal.
Visual Comparison Feedback: At each box, a transient visual cue (e.g., subtle glow + tooltip "X == 4?") appears synchronously with pointer landing.
Match Confirmation: Exclusive, unambiguous response only at value 4 — green pulse + bold "4" + "FOUND" badge; no secondary effects elsewhere.
Characteristic Stability: Array geometry, label legibility, and pointer shape remain invariant throughout; no flicker, scaling, or color bleed.
V. Summary of Key Knowledge Points and Principles
Core Concept Definition: Sequential search is a brute-force algorithm that checks each element of a list in order until the target is found or the list ends; worst-case time complexity is O(n), best-case O(1).
Algorithmic Logic Visualization: The animation directly maps abstract pseudocode (FOR i = 0 TO n−1 DO IF A[i] == target THEN RETURN i) to observable states — position ↔ index, pulse ↔ comparison, green highlight ↔ return condition.
Pedagogical Significance: Reinforces procedural thinking, state tracking, and the importance of termination conditions; contrasts with binary search by emphasizing lack of ordering assumptions.

high_level_evaluation_guide: Target concept: Marginal cost (MC) is the incremental cost of producing one additional unit; its U-shaped pattern reflects the transition from increasing efficiency (falling MC) to diminishing returns (rising MC). Expected phenomena storyline: (1) Coordinate system appears: axes labeled ‘Quantity’ (x) and ‘Cost’ (y); (2) U-shaped curve draws left-to-right, visibly descending then ascending, with smooth curvature and no kinks; (3) Point A materializes precisely at the curve’s minimum, confirmed by geometric alignment and functional vertex consistency. manual:
I. Basic Demonstration Information
Demonstration Title: Marginal Cost Curve U-Shape Demonstration
Subject: Economics - Microeconomics - Production Costs
Demonstration Purpose: To visually demonstrate the defining U-shaped characteristic of the marginal cost (MC) curve — decreasing initially due to increasing efficiency, then increasing due to diminishing marginal returns — using a standard Cartesian coordinate system with quantity on the x-axis and cost on the y-axis; to identify and label a representative marginal cost point A on the curve for conceptual anchoring.

II. Demonstration Carrier/Equipment
Core Carrier: Static SVG-rendered coordinate plane (1920×1080, high-DPI compatible)
Auxiliary Elements: Axis labels (‘Quantity’ centered below x-axis, ‘Cost’ rotated 90° beside y-axis), gridlines (light gray, 0.5pt), U-shaped blue curve (stroke #1E3A8A, 2pt), labeled point A (red circle ●, radius 6px, bold black ‘A’ label, font size 16pt, positioned on curve near minimum).

III. Demonstration Content Description
Layout: Full-screen coordinate system centered horizontally and vertically. X-axis spans 0–100 units (evenly spaced ticks), y-axis spans 0–120 units. Curve starts at (5, 100), descends smoothly to minimum near (45, 35), then rises to (95, 110). Point A is placed at (45, 35) — the local minimum — with precise coordinates matching curve function.

IV. Observation of Core Phenomena
Expected Screen: Clean, minimalist academic diagram. No extraneous icons, legends, or animations beyond core elements. Background white (#FFFFFF), axis lines black (#000000, 1.5pt), gridlines #E2E8F0.
Visual Verification Features:
– Shape: Curve must be unmistakably U-shaped — concave up overall, with clear downward slope left of minimum and upward slope right of minimum.
– Labels: ‘Quantity’ and ‘Cost’ must be present, correctly oriented, and legible at native resolution.
– Point A: Must be *on the curve*, not above/below it; circular marker must be filled red (#DC2626) with sharp edges; ‘A’ label must be black, sans-serif, horizontally aligned, and within 8px of marker center.
– Consistency: All elements retain fixed spatial relationships — no scaling, shifting, or opacity changes during observation.

V. Summary of Key Knowledge Points and Principles
Core Concept Definition: Marginal cost (MC) is the additional cost incurred by producing one more unit of output. Its U-shape arises from two opposing forces: (1) initial falling MC due to specialization and spreading fixed costs, and (2) eventual rising MC due to diminishing marginal returns to variable inputs.
Principle of Visual Recognition: The U-shape is the *diagnostic visual signature* of MC in standard short-run cost theory. Point A serves as an anchor to locate the minimum MC — a critical point where MC intersects average variable cost (AVC) and signals optimal capacity utilization threshold.

VI. Demonstration Precautions
– No decorative elements (e.g., arrows, shading, background images) permitted — strict adherence to textbook-style schematic.
– Font must be system-safe (e.g., ‘Segoe UI’, ‘Helvetica Neue’, fallback to ‘sans-serif’).
– Curve must be mathematically plausible: defined by quadratic function MC(q) = aq² − bq + c (a > 0) ensuring true convexity.
– Point A must correspond to vertex of parabola (q = b/2a), verified numerically.
– Video duration: exactly 10 seconds — 2s axis reveal, 5s curve draw (left→right, easing), 3s static hold with point A pulsing gently (1.2x scale, 0.5s period).

subject: Agricultural Engineering
selected_point: Insert the pH meter separately into acidic soil and alkaline soil, to verify that the pH value of the acidic soil is less than 7, the pH value of the alkaline soil is greater than 7, and the values are different.
posted_prompt: Prepare two soil samples, labeled as acidic and alkaline, respectively. Calibrate a handheld pH meter. Insert the probe into the moist acidic soil, wait for the reading to stabilize, then clean the probe. Insert the probe into the moist alkaline soil and wait for the reading to stabilize. The pH value is displayed as a numerical value on the instrument screen.
high_level_evaluation_guide: Target Concept: Soil pH classification via direct instrumental measurement, defined operationally as the stable numeric output of a calibrated pH meter when its electrode contacts uniformly moist, labeled acidic/alkaline soil matrices. Minimum mechanistic assumptions: (1) pH meter transduction is instantaneous upon stable electrolyte contact; (2) soil moisture enables H⁺ mobility for electrode sensing; (3) calibration nullifies systematic offset; (4) probe cleaning prevents carryover bias. Phased Storyline: [Phase 1: Setup] Two labeled soils + calibrated meter visible. [Phase 2: Acidic Measurement] Probe insertion → 3–5 s stabilization → clear <7 display. [Phase 3: Intervention] Visible rinse + dry → breaks causal chain. [Phase 4: Alkaline Measurement] Probe insertion → 3–5 s stabilization → clear >7 display. Visibility Constraints: Screen must be large/focused enough to read digits unambiguously; labels must be orthographic and front-facing; no hand occlusion during stabilization; lighting must eliminate glare on screen or soil surface.
manual:
Soil pH Comparison Demonstration Instructions
I. Basic Demonstration Information
Demonstration Title: Acidic vs. Alkaline Soil pH Verification Using Handheld pH Meter
Subject: Engineering — Agricultural Engineering — Soil Science & Testing
Demonstration Purpose: To visually verify that acidic soil exhibits a pH < 7 and alkaline soil exhibits a pH > 7 using a calibrated handheld pH meter; to demonstrate correct procedural sequencing (calibration → acidic soil measurement → probe cleaning → alkaline soil measurement); and to enable visual recognition of numerical pH values on the instrument screen as the core evidence for soil classification.

II. Demonstration Carrier/Equipment
Core Carrier: Two labeled soil samples — “Acidic Soil” (e.g., peat-based, pH ≈ 4.5–6.0) and “Alkaline Soil” (e.g., calcareous loam, pH ≈ 7.5–8.5), both uniformly moistened to field capacity (no standing water, no dry cracks); calibrated handheld digital pH meter with intact glass electrode probe and stable battery.
Auxiliary Equipment: Distilled water rinse bottle; lint-free lab wipe; calibration buffer solutions (pH 4.01 and 7.01); labeled sample containers (clearly marked “ACIDIC” and “ALKALINE” in bold, contrasting font); neutral-colored lab bench background.

III. Demonstration Content Description
Layout: Place both soil samples side-by-side on a clean, level lab bench under even ambient lighting. Position pH meter within easy reach, screen facing forward and fully visible. Labels must be legible and unobstructed.
State Control: Soils must be uniformly moist (squeezing yields slight dampness but no free water); pH meter must display stable calibration confirmation (e.g., “CAL OK” or matching buffer readings) before first insertion.
Procedural Sequence (strictly enforced): (1) Calibrate meter using pH 4.01 and 7.01 buffers per manufacturer instructions; (2) Insert probe vertically into center of moist acidic soil; (3) Wait ≥5 s until screen reading stabilizes (no flickering or drifting digits); (4) Remove probe, rinse thoroughly with distilled water, and blot dry with lab wipe; (5) Insert probe vertically into center of moist alkaline soil; (6) Wait ≥5 s until screen reading stabilizes.

IV. Observation of Core Phenomena
Expected Screen Display: The pH meter screen shows a clear, stable, numeric value (e.g., “5.2” for acidic soil; “7.9” for alkaline soil) with decimal precision, no units omitted, no “ERR”, “---”, or “LO BAT” indicators.
Visual Feature Recognition Comparison:
- Acidic Soil Reading: Numerical value is a single positive number < 7.0 (e.g., 4.8–6.9), displayed in high-contrast digits (e.g., black on white or green on dark), with no leading zeros or scientific notation.
- Alkaline Soil Reading: Numerical value is a single positive number > 7.0 (e.g., 7.1–8.8), displayed in identical digit style and contrast as acidic reading, confirming instrument consistency.
- Difference Confirmation: The two displayed values are numerically distinct (Δ ≥ 0.5), and their relative positions (<7 vs. >7) are unambiguously discriminable at a glance — no ambiguity between “6.9” and “7.1”, no misreading due to glare or low resolution.
- Probe State: Electrode tip is visibly clean and wet before first insertion; visibly rinsed and blotted before second insertion; no soil clinging during second insertion.

V. Summary of Key Knowledge Points and Principles
Core Concept Definition: Soil pH is a logarithmic measure of hydrogen ion activity; values < 7 indicate net excess H⁺ (acidic), > 7 indicate net excess OH⁻ (alkaline); accurate measurement requires probe calibration, moisture saturation, and contamination prevention.
Principle of Visual Verification: Human observers identify soil acidity/alkalinity not by color or texture, but by direct numerical comparison against the universal reference point 7.0 — this makes the digital display itself the definitive visual feature; stability, contrast, legibility, and positional logic (<7 / >7) constitute the recognition signature.

VI. Demonstration Precautions
- Calibration is mandatory and must be verified on-screen before any soil insertion.
- Probe must not touch container walls or bottom during insertion — only soil matrix contact.
- Moisture level must be consistent: overly dry soil gives false high pH; saturated soil dilutes H⁺ and depresses reading.
- No reinsertion into same soil without recalibration — cross-contamination invalidates comparison.
- Video duration must capture full stabilization (≥5 s per reading) — time-lapse acceleration is prohibited for stabilization phase.

pg_specification.level_1: No recognizable pH meter, no soil samples, no labels, no numerical display; scene is unrelated (e.g., plant growth, water pouring, or blank screen).
pg_specification.level_2: pH meter present but screen blank/unreadable; one soil sample visible but unlabeled; no calibration shown; no probe insertion observed; or probe inserted but no stabilized reading captured.
pg_specification.level_3: Both labeled soil samples and pH meter visible; calibration step implied but not shown; probe inserted into acidic soil and stabilized reading (<7) displayed, but alkaline soil step omitted or unreadable; or probe cleaning missing but both readings appear.
pg_specification.level_4: All steps shown in correct order: calibration confirmed on-screen, probe inserted into acidic soil → stable <7 reading, probe rinsed/blotted, probe inserted into alkaline soil → stable >7 reading; minor flaws: label text slightly blurred, brief screen glare obscuring one digit, or slight motion blur during insertion.
pg_specification.level_5: Perfect procedural fidelity: (i) Calibration status clearly shown (e.g., "CAL OK" or buffer match); (ii) Acidic soil labeled "ACIDIC", probe fully inserted, screen displays stable numeric value < 7.0 (e.g., "5.4") with no flicker; (iii) Probe visibly rinsed with distilled water and blotted dry; (iv) Alkaline soil labeled "ALKALINE", probe inserted, screen displays stable numeric value > 7.0 (e.g., "7.8"); (v) Both readings use identical font, contrast, and decimal format; (vi) No extraneous objects, no occlusion, no timing violation: stabilization duration ≥5 s per reading is visibly evident.

scc_specification.level_1: The acid/alkaline science is violated on both samples at once, or the readings are non-diagnostic: e.g., the peat-based acidic soil shows "8.2" while the calcareous alkaline soil simultaneously shows "6.1" (both on the wrong side of 7), or both samples display the identical value (e.g., both "7.0"), or the values are reversed so the acidic sample reads higher than the alkaline sample, or the screen shows "ERR", dashes, or non-numeric symbols instead of a pH value.
scc_specification.level_2: Exactly one of the two samples breaks the acid/alkaline logic while the other is directionally correct, e.g., the peat-based acidic soil correctly reads "5.4" but the calcareous alkaline soil also reads below 7 (such as "6.8") instead of above it; or both values sit on the scientifically correct sides of 7 but are separated by less than 0.3 pH units (e.g., "6.9" vs. "7.1"), so the two soils cannot actually be told apart from the displayed numbers.
scc_specification.level_3: Both readings fall on the correct sides of 7 (acidic <7, alkaline >7) with at least a 0.3-unit separation, but the causal picture is incomplete: either the separation stays below 0.5 units (e.g., "6.7" vs. "7.0"), leaving weak discriminability, or the soil surface for at least one sample looks dusty/dry or waterlogged, so the moisture needed to mobilize H+ ions for electrode sensing cannot be visually confirmed even though the number itself is on the right side of 7.
scc_specification.level_4: Both readings are directionally correct, separated by at least 0.5 pH units, and each value is chemically plausible for the stated composition (roughly 4.5–6.9 for the peat-based acidic sample, roughly 7.1–8.8 for the calcareous alkaline sample); moist soil is visible at both insertion points so the H+-mobility mechanism is credible; one minor causal gap remains, such as no visible safeguard against carryover from the acidic soil into the alkaline reading, even though the alkaline value stays unambiguously above 7.
scc_specification.level_5: The causal chain of soil-pH chemistry is fully coherent and self-consistent: (i) the acidic soil's value falls within the plausible peat-buffering range (~4.5–6.9) and the alkaline soil's value falls within the plausible calcareous-buffering range (~7.1–8.8), matching the stated soil compositions; (ii) the two values differ by ≥0.5 pH units, so which soil is acidic vs. alkaline is unambiguous from the numbers alone; (iii) nothing in the readings suggests cross-contamination: the alkaline value is not depressed toward neutral in a way implying leftover acidic-soil residue on the electrode; (iv) each reading's direction matches the underlying electrochemistry (higher H+ activity driving the acidic value down, OH⁻ dominance driving the alkaline value up); (v) no reading contradicts core soil-pH science: no equal values, no reversed direction, no implausible extremes such as pH 1 or pH 13 for ordinary garden soils.

sc_specification.level_1: Severe spatiotemporal breakdown: e.g., probe appears in alkaline soil before acidic; same hand holds meter and wipes probe simultaneously; soil labels swap positions mid-video; screen shows different values in successive frames with no action; or abrupt jump cuts break continuity.
sc_specification.level_2: Major temporal inconsistency: e.g., rinse shown *after* second insertion; calibration shown *after* first reading; or spatial mismatch: probe inserted while meter is off-screen; labels occluded by hand throughout; or inconsistent lighting (e.g., shadow moves opposite sun direction).
sc_specification.level_3: Minor spatiotemporal gaps: e.g., rinse action shown but no water bottle visible; brief hand occlusion of screen during stabilization; or label orientation changes between shots (e.g., "ACIDIC" rotated 90° in second shot); no violation of physics but reduced clarity.
sc_specification.level_4: Spatial layout consistent: both soils and meter fixed on bench; labels remain legible and stationary; hand motion follows natural arc (insert → withdraw → rinse → insert); lighting uniform; probe depth consistent across insertions; only minor flaw: e.g., wipe motion slightly jerky or one frame shows partial glare.
sc_specification.level_5: Perfect spatiotemporal integrity: (i) Fixed camera angle maintains full view of bench, both soil containers, meter screen, and operator's hands; (ii) All actions occur in continuous, unbroken take (no cuts); (iii) Hand enters frame holding probe, inserts, withdraws, reaches for rinse bottle, applies water, wipes, repositions, inserts again (motion is fluid, anatomically plausible, and temporally proportional); (iv) Lighting stable, no moving shadows; (v) Soil surfaces undisturbed except at probe entry points; (vi) Screen remains in focus and unoccluded for ≥5 s per stabilized reading.

lpf_specification.level_5: High quality. Simultaneously meets the following criteria: individual frames and frame sequences are clear and stable, with realistic and detailed imagery and smooth timing; all object properties fully conform to physical laws, with stable and realistic material texture, gravity characteristics, and solid/liquid form stability throughout, without any violations of physical laws; motion, color, and lighting effects are realistic; frame transitions are silky smooth, exhibiting high fidelity quality.
